title: Ferdinand III to Hatzfeldt, Regensburg, August-September 1641: the clear texts of Stützel's group I (read in part, 94.1% of cipher words; letter of 14 Sept. read)

documents.shelfmark: Neuenstein, Hohenlohe-Zentralarchiv (Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg), Ni 10 (Rosenberg-Hatzfeldt) Bd 242, fols. 46r-49v

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the documents. Key and method published by Stützel 1963 (Anlage 1), who says the 1641 letters could all be translated, but prints none of their clear texts.

transcription.source: HZA Neuenstein reproduction order LABW-6aeaff73efe93 (19 images, 200 dpi), private research copies, not published
transcription.notes: Sign by sign by seven Claude Opus agents without key values, frozen (SHA-256) before decoding; then reviewed on the images for the b/u (TAU/CROSSO, 37 signs) and x/y (VEN/MER, 19 signs) confusions; a second, blind transcriber redid one page per hand (7 pages, 1,576 tokens): 91.5% identical tokens, 94.4% same key value; the 18 unresolved signs were then shown to Brice Dudout in a blind, pre-registered review (one sign per question, shapes only): 7 tokens changed, 11 confirmed (CORRECTIONS-T3.tsv).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution with nulls (Stützel 1963, group I): zodiac signs a-m in order, ◡ n, astrological aspects o-r, planets and Moon s-z, with numerals as homophones of vowels (3 10 25 = a, 7 8 65 = e, 5 70 81 = i, 30 = o, 4 = u) and ten nulls (o‡, [·], ПП, ×, Z, 79, 89, 91, 94, 961); signs separated by dots, no word division. Key published by Stützel (key.tsv).

prior_solution.where: H. Stützel, "Chiffrierwesen im Dreißigjährigen Krieg", Württembergisch Franken 47 (1963) 109-115 (DOI 10.53458/wfr.v47i.13761, CC BY 4.0): key of group I (Anlage 1) and method; no clear text of the 1641 letters printed. Checked: this repository (no target, catalogue entry or lead for Neuenstein Ni 10 or Stützel; GitHub API, origin/main c786648b, 5 Nov 2026), research/leads.json, DECODE, web search (no edition; Deutsche Reichstagsakten 1640/41 digital edition in preparation, not checked).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout ordered the reproductions from the HZA, found Stützel 1963 and set the rules (key frozen as printed, transcription frozen before decoding, Daniel's counting rule, a targeted blind review of doubtful signs). AI agents transcribed, decoded, read, counted and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Stützel 1963 identified as the prior work on the Neuenstein Hatzfeldt letters: four systems broken, keys printed; group I = Ferdinand III to Hatzfeld 1641 = Bd 242.

Stützel's key I, transcribed from the article and frozen, applied to an independent transcription of fol. 90r: C1 1.00, trigram score -2.66 vs 200 shuffled-key controls max -3.20; 0.977 of 220 letters read as German.

All 381 cipher lines (5,519 signs, 19 images) transcribed sign by sign without key values and frozen; a second blind transcriber redid one page per hand (7 pages): 91.5% identical tokens, 94.4% same key value; the gap is mostly in null shapes and in the hand of the postscript.

Systematic confusions reviewed on the images: 37 signs transcribed TAU (b) where the sense wants u are single-loop CROSSO (u); 10 signs transcribed VEN (x) where the sense wants y are 8-shaped MER (y), 9 more left as VEN|MER; 3 u-for-r in P4 are looped signs, not misread stars (left restored).

Five pieces decoded with the key unchanged and read by Daniel's rule (after the blind review): 859 cipher words, 677 certain, 131 probable, 49 restored, 2 unresolved = 94.1% (letters: 98.9%); the letter of 14 Sept. reaches 95.3%.

The 18 unresolved signs shown to Brice Dudout in a blind, pre-registered review (shapes from the same hand, neutral ids, consequences fixed before the answers). 7 tokens changed (4 -> JUP, a dot before a null [·], ARI -> SUN, two numbers in clear 24 and 14, ? -> SAT, 8 -> TAU), 11 confirmed. Read: 90v 'konnest', 'vom 24 Augusti', 'innerhalb 14 Tagen', 101v 'selbige spesa' (shape SAT chosen; the remark 'looks like a 5' describes that shape). Still unresolved: 4 letters of the postscript, 2 letters of a marginal insertion.

outcome.method_basis: Stützel's printed key (1963, Anlage 1) applied unchanged to a fresh transcription of Bd 242; clear texts not previously published.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (reading.md, NOTES.md): 859 cipher words, 677 certain, 131 probable, 49 restored, 2 unresolved; certain + probable = 808/859. By letters 4,970/5,027 = 98.9%.

texts.label: 21 Aug 1641 (fols. 46r-49v)
texts.summary: Ferdinand III approves Hatzfeldt's plan for after the siege of Dorsten, has told Archduke Leopold Wilhelm to send him orders, and promises provisions, ammunition, foot, the Mandelsloh regiment and sixty Austrian ox-wagons for his march to Franconia.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (reading agent, for Brice Dudout); prudent grade B, not yet confirmed by Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Read as sentences after the blind review of the 18 unresolved signs. Words: 122 certain, 38 probable, 12 restored, 0 unresolved of 172 = 93.0%; letters: 958/971 = 98.7%. Graded B, not A: one AI reader saw the decryption; the clear passages have not been checked by a human palaeographer; under 95% of words read.

texts.label: 7 Sept 1641 (fols. 90r-90v)
texts.summary: Preparations for the operation against Erfurt are under way (provisions from Leipzig); once Dorsten has fallen Hatzfeldt is to bring two half-cannon from "Statt Berg" and find horses to draw them.

texts.label: 14 Sept 1641 (fols. 97r-105v)
texts.summary: The Emperor lists the guns, powder, grain and wagons gathered at Würzburg and Leipzig for the Erfurt operation, urges Hatzfeldt not to delay after Dorsten, asks the Cardinal-Infante through Traun for 120,000 guilders owed to the Westphalian corps, and encloses the Aachen bond.

reading_review.by: Brice Dudout (grade confirmed 5 Nov 2026); reading by Claude Opus 5.5
reading_review.note: Read as sentences after the blind review of the 18 unresolved signs. Words: 382 certain, 64 probable, 21 restored, 1 unresolved of 468 = 95.3%; letters: 2706/2729 = 99.2%. The two numbers read from Brice Dudout's remarks (24, 14) count: with one of them left unresolved, 95.1%; with both, 94.9%. Graded A by Brice Dudout, who did the blind review of the unresolved signs; the piece is at the 95% line (95.1% with one of the two numbers from the blind review left open, 94.9% with both).
